fact_text:
Ireland's employment-permit lodgement rule (12 weeks before the proposed start) and the subsequent employment-visa decision (approximately 8 weeks) are sequential, not concurrent. Adding those two already-published figures gives approximately 20 weeks before the proposed start that a third-country national who needs both a permit and an entry visa should treat as the combined runway.

The 12-week figure is DETE's lodgement rule, copied from the existing ReloPass requirement ES_IE:THIRD_COUNTRY:permit_application_12_week_lead_time. It is not a processing estimate.

The approximately-8-week visa decision, and applying up to 3 months before travel, are copied from the existing ReloPass requirement ES_IE:THIRD_COUNTRY:entry_visa_after_permit_timing. They are not stated in that row's ISD evidence quote. The ISD page only supports the sequence: once the permit is granted, the person may apply for an Employment Visa. This composed requirement does not invent a new statutory 20-week figure.

non_obvious_note.official_guidance: Lodge the employment permit at least 12 weeks before the start date; apply for an employment visa once you hold a permit.
non_obvious_note.actual_reality: The permit (DETE) and the visa (ISD) run one after the other. Treating 12 weeks as the whole runway understates the wait by the visa decision (~8 weeks on the existing visa-timing requirement).
non_obvious_note.action_required: Work the agreed start date backwards from approximately 20 weeks when both a permit and an entry visa are required; do not overlap the two waits.

evidence_quote: An application for any employment permit must be received at least 12 weeks before the proposed employment start date.

additional_citations.name: Immigration Service Delivery — Employment visa
additional_citations.evidence_quote: Once you have received a permit, you are eligible to apply for an Employment Visa.
